claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or nanoribbons have high residual stress.
The as-deposited material has a fine, possibly defect-rich grain structure.
Nanoscale effects constrain magnetic-domain dynamics in the as-deposited material.
Rapid thermal annealing relieves residual stress in the FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Rapid thermal annealing modifies grain structure and grain-boundary density or morphology.
Stress relief and grain-structure modification reduce domain-wall pinning sites.
Reduced pinning improves magnetic-domain-wall mobility and domain alignment.
Improved domain-wall mobility permits easier domain reorientation under applied fields below 100 mT.
Annealing-induced microstructural changes improve local thermal transport or thermal coupling within the material.
Improved domain mobility and thermal coupling produce more effective coupling between magnetic and thermal processes.
Annealed samples will have lower coercivity and smaller magnetic-hysteresis loop area than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit a greater adiabatic temperature change and/or magnetic entropy change than as-deposited samples.
The as-deposited nanoscale material has an inferior magnetocaloric response relative to bulk counterparts.
Heat-transfer rate is a significant operating constraint in these nanoscale geometries.
The proposed effect is applicable below 100 mT and within an annealing window that avoids phase changes.
The proposed effect may not hold under high-field or bulk-material conditions.
The magnitude of coercivity reduction and magnetocaloric enhancement depends on the annealing parameters and resulting microstructure.
XRD and TEM can be used to assess relevant microstructural changes, although the cited evidence does not establish their use for residual-stress measurement in this alloy.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis decrease and an improved magnetocaloric response despite confirmed microstructural modification would falsify the hypothesis.
